answer: A kiln yard stays honest when every new identity must tend a distinct ember in a different kiln, feeding it fuel bundles gathered one at a time from a shrinking woodlot while a warden watches the ripple of heat on the river. The first fake owes one bundle, the second four, the third nine, since the nth fake owes the square of its number, so the tenth fake alone owes a hundred bundles. Bulk farming fails since one gatherer carries a single bundle per trip down the narrow bank path and kilns cannot share fuel, like one potter firing one kiln per dawn as the beacon glow marks each kiln.
